root_motivation: Running daemons can silently execute stale binaries after reinstalls — nothing on this laptop detects it automatically. The self-review journal re-discovers the same 'agorabus stale binary' finding every tick because no tool computes the verdict. binstale makes this a single CLI invocation rather than a recurring manual investigation.
user_persona: Joe Yen running ~/wintermute system daemons (agorabus, recalld, wm-*) on Arch Linux. Runs binstale from self-review hooks or interactively to check whether long-running processes are executing binaries that have been reinstalled underneath them.

acceptance_criteria.description: `binstale check <pid>` against a process whose /proc/PID/exe readlink ends in ' (deleted)' returns verdict `deleted-exe` and exit code 1. Test: fork from temp binary, unlink it, check child PID.

`binstale check <pid>` against a process whose backing binary was replaced via atomic rename returns `inode-drift` verdict. Test: copy sleeper to tmp, exec it, rename new copy over path, check running PID.
`binstale check <pid>` against a process whose binary is unchanged since exec returns `fresh` and exit code 0. Test: spawn a long-sleep process from an unmodified binary.

`binstale scan --match '^sleep$'` (or a controlled regex) lists one row per matching process with a verdict column; `--format json` emits valid JSON with documented keys: pid, comm, exe_path, exe_inode, ondisk_inode, prov_ts, proc_start, verdict, evidence.
When on-disk binary has no user.prov.* xattr, binstale does not error — it falls back to mtime and records prov_ts: null in JSON.
`binstale check <nonexistent-pid>` exits 2 with a clear stderr message and emits no partial JSON.
Unit tests for the verdict classifier (pure-function tests over synthetic ProcInfo structs) pass: deleted_exe, inode_drift, prov_stale, fresh cases each covered.
`binstale --help`, `binstale scan --help` document every flag and the verdict taxonomy; `binstale --version` returns `binstale 0.1.0`.

scope: Read /proc/PID/exe via readlink to detect (deleted) suffix
Compare exe inode vs on-disk inode via stat calls to detect inode-drift
Read user.prov.ts xattr from on-disk binary; fall back to mtime
Read process start time from /proc/PID/stat field 22 + /proc/stat btime + sysconf(CLK_TCK)
Classify each process as: deleted-exe | inode-drift | prov-stale | fresh
binstale check <pid> subcommand for single-process verdict
binstale scan --match <regex> subcommand scanning /proc/*/comm and cmdline
non_goals: Never restarts, reinstalls, or signals any process — detection only
No async runtime (tokio) — synchronous /proc reads only
No remote process inspection — only local /proc filesystem
No continuous monitoring or daemon mode — one-shot invocation only
No stale shared-library detection (only executable binary staleness)

additional.no_tokio: synchronous /proc reads only; no async runtime
additional.linux_only: uses /proc filesystem and Linux xattr APIs

five_whys_trace.q: Why do you need a tool to detect stale running binaries?
five_whys_trace.a: The agorabus daemon (pid 2138939) is executing a binary whose inode was unlinked at 20:52 reinstall, but the process is still running the old code. /proc/2138939/exe shows '(deleted)'.

five_whys_trace.q: Why does it matter that agorabus is running a deleted binary?
five_whys_trace.a: A reinstall may fix a bug or change behavior, but the running daemon silently ignores the fix until restarted. Every tick that talks to a stale agorabus gets the old behavior without knowing it.

five_whys_trace.q: Why is the current self-review finding it manually every time rather than automatically?
five_whys_trace.a: No tool computes the staleness verdict. The run-18 journal notes this is the third time across runs 16-18 it was discovered manually — three consecutive self-review cycles burned on the same re-discovery.

five_whys_trace.q: Why not just check /proc/*/exe for '(deleted)' in a shell one-liner?
five_whys_trace.a: The (deleted) suffix is only one staleness signal. Atomic rename replaces the inode without leaving (deleted). And provfs xattr provides a third independent signal when the inode is ambiguous. A single shell grep misses two of the three cases.

ambiguities_resolved.question: Does prov-stale require provfs LSM to be running?
ambiguities_resolved.resolution: Graceful fallback: when user.prov.ts xattr is absent (provfs not running or filesystem doesn't support xattrs), fall back to comparing on-disk mtime vs proc_start. prov_ts: null in JSON output. Never error on absent xattr.

ambiguities_resolved.question: What exit code when scan finds zero matching processes?
ambiguities_resolved.resolution: Exit 0 (no stale processes found — empty set is fresh). Only exit 1 when ≥1 verdict is non-fresh.
